mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite elevated FEDFUNDS, or FEDFUNDS stays above 4% for <30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in labor participation (UNRATE) creates a dual labor market stress that is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases while UNRATE also decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns turn positive when labor indicators normalize or diverge in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST, INDPRO) in the prior quarter coincides with a decline in supply indicators (RSAFS), signaling an inventory buildup that suppresses near-term equity valuations and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_prev * 1.10 and RSAFS < RSAFS_prev over the same quarter
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when demand and supply indicators revert to equilibrium.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth (2% monthly yoy) over three months is accompanied by a flattening of capacity utilization (not in observable list - so omit interaction), predicting positive 60-day SPX returns as market anticipates supply expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day returns underperform a 5% moving average baseline during the INDPRO acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a tighter policy path, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when inflation reverts to 2% or below within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (PAYEMS) below 4,000 followed by a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a regime shift to labor market weakness that is associated with negative 5-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 4000 and UNRATE > UNRATE_prev in the same week
failure_condition: 5-day returns turn positive when labor indicators stabilize or improve.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not available - so use HOUST as proxy for demand) and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicate demand pullback, which is associated with negative 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_prev * 1.03 and INDPRO < INDPRO_prev over the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when demand indicators recover and INDPRO rebounds.

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of FEDFUNDS is above 4% and UNRATE is below 5%, the combination of higher discount rates and weaker labor market expectations is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 6-month MA(FEDFUNDS) > 4% and UNRATE < 5% over the same period
failure_condition: 60-day returns are non-negative when policy is restrictive and labor is strong.
